stories.title: Firefighters celebrate rain during Indonesia wildfires
summary: A number of clips show firefighters celebrating in the rain.

stories.title: BBC Inside Science
summary: Time is running out for one of the most ambitious environmental pledges in history.

stories.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms
summary: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may connect several seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity.
The surprising discovery could help explain the disorder's underlying mechanisms and potentially lead to earlier detection and new treatments.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging.
Six popular sweeteners were linked to faster cognitive decline, raising concerns about the long-term brain health effects of common sugar substitutes, although causation was not established.

stories.title: South West Water given lowest environmental rating
summary: The water firm is performing "significantly below target" for pollution, the Environment Agency says.

stories.title: A 700,000-year-old elephant tooth reveals a lost world where early humans lived
summary: A remarkably preserved elephant tooth dating back nearly 700,000 years has revealed a surprisingly lush prehistoric world where giant elephants and early humans lived side by side.
Discovered in northern Israel alongside ancient stone tools, the tooth belonged to a straight-tusked elephant, one of the largest land mammals of the Ice Age.

stories.title: NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
summary: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind.
The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.

stories.title: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment
summary: All but one of England's water companies were rated as "poor" or "requiring improvement" for environmental targets.

stories.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
summary: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy.

Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity.
The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.

stories.title: Mini-gardens for bees on bus stop roofs approved
summary: Living Roofs aimed at boosting biodiversity in urban areas will be installed under a new bus stop contract.

stories.title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
summary: Getting more daylight could be linked to a surprisingly powerful benefit for brain health.

In a study of more than 87,000 adults, researchers found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia, with longer exposure to bright light linked to even greater reductions.
Remarkably, getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.

stories.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history
summary: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet may be more than 128,000 years old, preserving an extraordinary record of Earth's climate that scientists previously thought had been lost.
The discovery reveals a rare glimpse into the last ice age and could reshape our understanding of how glaciers survive dramatic changes in global climate.

stories.title: RAF base chemical contamination worst in UK, report says
summary: Testing at RAF Upper Heyford finds "unacceptable" levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

stories.title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
summary: Researchers have discovered a small group of brain cells that prevents dangerous blood pressure swings, even when average readings appear normal.
The finding reveals a hidden source of cardiovascular risk and could open the door to new treatments that protect the heart and brain.

stories.title: Scientists just broke a textbook rule of physics
summary: Scientists have defied a long-standing rule of laser physics by generating X-rays with much higher energies than conventional theory predicts.
The surprising discovery reveals how two electrons working together can overcome a previously accepted limit, opening new possibilities for quantum research.

stories.title: Meteors don't just burn up. What really happens is far more violent
summary: Scientists have uncovered seven surprising stages that space rocks go through as they hurtle toward Earth, revealing that melting and violent fragmentation, rather than simple evaporation, determine their fate.
The discovery could help explain why meteorites scatter across the ground and how dangerous asteroids explode in Earth's atmosphere.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
summary: Scientists have discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen, potentially revealing a hidden contributor to our planet's oxygen-rich atmosphere.
The findings suggest that ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.

stories.title: Scientists discover a secret glow in toxic fire salamanders
summary: Researchers have discovered a surprising hidden ability in Europe's familiar black-and-yellow fire salamanders: they glow green and cyan under ultraviolet light.
The mysterious fluorescence comes mainly from glands in their skin and their toxic secretions, which can continue glowing for more than 24 hours after being released.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden 100-million-year-old volcanic system
summary: Scientists have uncovered a long-lost volcanic system in Iran that dates back roughly 100 million years, revealing a hidden chapter in Earth's tectonic history.
The discovery sheds new light on the disappearance of an ancient ocean and the powerful geological forces that reshaped the Middle East.

stories.title: Earth's ice ages may have been driven by a hidden ocean chain reaction
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising connection between Earth's opposite poles that may help explain how the planet plunged into past ice ages.
New research suggests that as massive ice sheets expanded across the Northern Hemisphere, they cooled Atlantic Ocean waters that eventually traveled south toward Antarctica.
This cooling may have disrupted Southern Ocean circulation, allowing the ocean to absorb and store more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, further cooling the planet.

stories.title: NASA’s Artemis I mission reveals surprising radiation levels near the Moon
summary: NASA’s Artemis I mission has revealed that cosmic radiation near the Moon is higher than in Earth orbit, but not by as much as scientists might expect.
Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.
